name: Citi
seo_title: Citi online assessment and interviews: what to expect
description: What Citi's own careers pages say about its online assessments, interviews and final stage, each line linked to its source.
intro: This guide sums up what Citi's own careers pages say about applying and interviewing, from how to apply to insight programmes and staying in touch. It reflects those pages as we checked them on 16 October 2026. Processes differ by programme, role and country, so check Citi's careers site for your role before you apply.

items.text: Citi says its early career application process has five steps: apply, skills evaluation, first interview, final stage and, if you are the best fit, an offer.
Citi says you start by applying through its online portal, and asks you to highlight your skills and relevant experience.

Citi says Workday is its main platform for all recruitment, including programme applications and event registrations, and that you must create a new Citi-specific Workday account, because accounts made for other companies cannot be used.
Citi says applications for its Summer Analyst internships, which are for penultimate-year university students, usually open in September of the year before the internship starts in May or June.

For its 2027 Summer Analyst role in the Investment Banking Real Estate team in London, Citi says it recruits on a rolling basis, has no application deadline and encourages you to apply as soon as possible.

For its 2027 Markets Sales and Trading Summer Analyst programme in London, Citi says that after you apply you will be asked to choose your preferred area of Markets (Sales, Trading, Structuring, Quantitative Analysis, or Securitisation and Financing), and it uses your answer to place you in the most suitable recruitment process.

Citi says official recruitment emails may come from addresses ending in @citi.com or @talentintelligence.citi.com, or from citi@myworkday.com, and that its authorised partners may also contact candidates from their own domains. It says it will never ask candidates to pay for training, software, work equipment, visas or administrative fees; background check fees may apply in some cases, but only after a formal offer.
Citi says the skills evaluation step is a skills discovery survey for EMEA and global Services programmes, or an assessment of your coding skills for Tech programmes.

For its 2027 Investment Banking Summer Internship Programme in Tokyo, which is for students at overseas universities and Japanese students on exchange abroad, Citi says applicants are invited to a web-based assessment within about five business days of applying, and the application is not complete until the assessment is done.

For its 2027 Markets Summer Internship Programme in Tokyo (recruited at the Boston Career Forum 2026), Citi says applicants are invited to a web-based test within 10 business days of applying, and that candidates who have completed it are then told about the next steps.
Citi says that if you are selected, you will be invited to a one-on-one first interview that looks more closely at your background and how your aims fit with Citi's.
Citi says interviews may be held by phone, by video or in person, depending on the role and location, and that it does not hire only through messaging apps.

Citi says its 2027 Citi Research Summer Analyst role in London is a Certified Role under the FCA and PRA Certification Regime, so candidates are assessed as fit and proper through extensive interviews, self-disclosures, criminal record, reference and credit checks, and other background screening.
For its 2027 Technology Cyber Security Summer Analyst role in Warsaw, Citi lists the ability to pass technical interviews built around basic algorithmic programming exercises.
Citi says that, depending on the programme and location, the final stage is either multiple interviews, an assessment or a case study exercise.
Citi says that if you are the best fit for the role it will contact you with an offer, and your recruiter will give you the details.
Citi says official offers are always made in writing through authorised Citi channels, followed by a secure onboarding process.

For its 2027 Summer Analyst role in the Investment Banking Real Estate team in London, Citi asks for students in their penultimate or final year of university with an expected or achieved 2:1 (or equivalent) at undergraduate level in any degree subject and an interest in business, and says a second language is desirable but not essential.

For its 2027 London Investment Banking Real Estate Summer Analyst role, Citi says it looks for intellectual curiosity, strong communication, planning and organisational skills, a wish to understand the financial industry deeply, and a commitment to integrity and ethical decision-making.

For its 2027 Markets Sales and Trading Summer Analyst programme in London, Citi asks for a good understanding of finance, an interest in Markets and proficiency in Microsoft Office, especially Excel, and says knowledge of VBA or Python is highly desirable.

sections.heading: Insight programmes and staying in touch

items.text: For its London Citi Insight Program hosted by the Social Mobility Network, Citi says the programme includes interview preparation and that successful candidates can interview for the London summer analyst programmes.

Citi says its four-day London Spring Insight programme is for students in the first year of a three-year course or the second year of a four-year undergraduate course, that applications open in October or November, and that it prepares participants for a pipeline into its Summer Internship opportunities, subject to performance.
For its US Early Identification programme, Citi says it offers interview preparation for Summer Analyst roles.
Citi suggests staying connected during your job search by following Citi Careers on social media, joining its talent community and attending its virtual or in-person recruitment events.

practice_advice: Practise explaining a client situation and your recommendation out loud in a few minutes, with the answer first and then your reasons.
Keep a short list of business stories you have followed, and practise saying what each one means for a company and its bank.
Do short, timed mental maths drills most days: the numbers in a case study are easier when the arithmetic is automatic.
